findings.title: Silence action is rendered but cannot open its drawer for Prometheus-only list rules
findings.body: The list now supplies only `promRule` for Grafana rules, so `AlertRuleMenu` can correctly enable and render “Silence notifications” from the new Prometheus-rule ability. Clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer`, but the drawer is only rendered when a ruler alerting rule is present. For every Grafana rule in the new list this condition is false, making the visible silence menu item a no-op.

findings.title: Delete is hidden for Grafana rules after removing ruler data
findings.body: `canDelete` now includes the Prometheus-rule permission result, but the delete menu item still additionally requires `rulerRule`. `GrafanaRuleListItem` invokes this menu with only `promRule`, so users with delete permission never receive a Delete action in the alert list. The delete handler already closes over the identifier in `RuleActionsButtons`, so the ruler-rule guard prevents an otherwise available operation.

findings.title: Pause is hidden for every Grafana rule in the ruler-free list
findings.body: The new Grafana Prometheus ability can make `canPause` true, but rendering the pause item still requires a `rulerRule`. The new list intentionally provides no ruler rule, so pausable Grafana-managed rules no longer expose a pause/unpause action there despite the permissions calculation indicating that the action is supported and allowed.

findings.title: Federated ruler rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: The previous ability implementation called `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and disabled mutable actions for federated groups. This replacement unconditionally sets `isFederated` to false because it no longer receives the group. Consequently edit, delete, pause, restore, and related actions can be presented for federated external rule groups that were previously intentionally immutable; attempting them may fail server-side or permit unsupported edits.

findings.title: Grafana rule list items no longer have React keys
findings.body: The old `GrafanaRuleLoader` received `key={key}`, but the replacement `GrafanaRuleListItem` is returned without a key. Multiple Grafana results in the `<ul>` therefore trigger React's missing-key warning and are reconciled by position, which can cause stateful child UI (such as an opened action menu) to be associated with the wrong rule when result ordering changes or additional batches are inserted.
